creator: kamchai
summary: A fast Thai explainer about a product or tool, built on a split screen. B-roll fills the top half and the speaker (seated, mic in shot, bookshelf behind) sits in the bottom half. The hook opens split, with a 2-3 row Thai title in heavy white type (one phrase in yellow) sitting on the bottom edge of the B-roll just above the seam, plus the product's name or logo on the footage. After that the reel alternates every 3-9 s between three layouts. Split blocks have a one-line Thai caption on a translucent dark strip exactly on the seam (y≈50 %). Full-frame speaker blocks have no captions; one big punch phrase sits on the chest (y≈61-65 %, keyword in yellow). Occasional full-frame B-roll carries a centred white phrase. A recurring label puts a white line over the head with black text on a yellow box under it. Cuts are very frequent (36-46/min, median shot 1.2-1.4 s), the voice has no pauses at all, and the reel can end on a comment-keyword CTA with the creator's handle.

fit_notes: The split needs B-roll for about half the reel. With no product footage, use stock only for illustrative shots and mark the product-label device 'ask'.
Reach 36-46 cuts/min with zoom.snaps and B-roll changes, not by cutting words.
Thai rows: break only at phrase ends; seam captions ≤ 17 chars/s and ≤ 35 chars per line (METHOD F2-F3).
